rationale: The Latin anchors *fragorem edere* (to make a crashing/cracking noise), *sonare* (to sound), and *crepare* (to crack/burst) point to a sudden breaking apart with noise, which best matches the intransitive "become separated into pieces or fragments" sense (break.v.02). The attestations from Beowulf and Exodus similarly suggest physical bursting or cracking asunder rather than a transitive destruction sense.
